content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text counts Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 toward a broken link, so K-G4 governs whether those verses can be counted that way.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and Matthew 1:25 \"knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" contradict C3's claim of espousal union", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way.", "room": "The phrase 'counts toward a broken link' could mean any verse used to break the link, or only verses expressly labeled unanswered witnesses; I read it as any verse used toward the broken link because the rule says such a verse is counted this way.", "why": "The judge uses Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 to declare the challenger link broken, but neither quotes an earlier-round sentence pressing them against that link nor names the round, so counting them breaches K-G4."}
